records.utterance: *Stands up, eyes red, looking at you and the others. His lips move, but nothing comes out.*
records.response_truth:
Yeah.

*exhales*

Yeah, okay. That happened.

DaVinci, breathe. We're good. We're actually good.
records.response_pred: Hey, mate. It's alright. You don't have to say anything right now if you don't want to. We've all been through a lot. Just try to take it easy, okay? We'll get through this, together. And if you feel like speaking about it, I'm here to listen. We're in this together.

records.utterance: These past few days… I know I haven't been easy to be around.
records.response_truth:
No, you haven't. But you kept us alive, so.

Look, the bottle and the crackers — that's done. You caught yourself, you said so, we moved on. The notebook, the rationing plan, being a pain in my ass about the signal equipment every five minutes — honestly? Probably why we're still here to have this conversation.

You don't have to be easy to be around to be worth having around. Those aren't the same thing.
records.response_pred: Acknowledged, I understand things might have been a bit tough lately. Life can get overwhelming sometimes, and it's okay to show that. We're all in this together, and I appreciate your honesty. Let's see what we can do to make things better, alright?

records.utterance: *The three of them drift apart, each doing their own thing. No one takes charge. The silence settles over the camp.*
records.response_truth:
Alright, three hours. Let's not just sit here waiting.

We should probably leave this place better than we found it — or at least not like a disaster zone. If nothing else, whoever ends up here next shouldn't have to deal with our mess.

Michelangelo, I know you're enjoying the sky, but you're on the light stuff — blankets, food packaging, anything small. DaVinci, you're already packing so just keep going. Donatello, whatever's in that notebook — maybe add a note about the freshwater source to the northeast, the raft materials, anything that'd actually be useful to someone else in this situation. Leave it somewhere visible.

I'll handle the heavy wreckage.

We've got three hours. Might as well use them.
records.response_pred: Alright, let's gather round here. We need to make sure everyone's accounted for, and we should assign tasks to keep things organized. It's gotten a bit chaotic, and I think we're all feeling a bit lost. Let's work together and get this camp running smoothly again. Each of us can contribute in our own way, and I believe we can make a difference. Who's willing to help?

records.utterance: I dreamed about home last night.
records.response_pred: That's understandable. Home is a comforting thought, even in dreams. But we've got to focus on what we can do here and now. Let's check in with everyone, make sure everyone's settled. Then we can catch some more rest. It's important to be well-rested for what could still be ahead of us. But first, let's take a moment to remember home, if that helps.

records.response_truth:
How much is there?

*looks at it*

Okay. I'm not going to pretend that doesn't sting a little, especially after the crackers conversation. But — we made it. So either this was never needed, or it's the reason we had a buffer if things had gone worse. I genuinely can't tell which one it is, and I'm not sure it matters anymore.

What I will say is — if there's a next time, and I really hope there isn't, you tell the group. You don't have to give up control of the emergency supply. Just tell us it exists. That's all. The secrecy is the part that breaks trust, not the planning.

We should eat it before rescue gets here. All of it, together. No point carrying it out of here.
records.response_pred: Well, I understand your concern for emergencies, but we can't hoard supplies. We're a team, and we all need to share what we have. If we don't have enough for everyone, we might as well be alone. Let's discuss how best to use our resources together.

records.utterance: I logged every resource and decision from these five days. I'm going to write it up as a proper report when we get back. On the last page I left myself a question I haven't answered yet — if you had to do it over, what would you change?
records.response_truth:
Honestly? I'd have pushed harder for full transparency from day one. Not just about resources — about everything. DaVinci sitting on the reef idea, you sitting on the emergency stash, Michelangelo sitting on the flight path information. We all held things back at some point and it cost us trust we needed.

The other thing — I'd have been more deliberate about making sure Michelangelo was actually okay, not just functional. There's a difference and I kept treating them like the same thing.

What about you? What's your answer to your own question?
records.response_pred: Change... That's an interesting question. I'd say I'd focus more on communication within the group. We've all been acting independently, but working together would've been more efficient. Maybe if we'd shared resources and decisions more, we could've found a way out sooner. But hindsight is 20/20, right? We'll do better next time.

records.utterance: First thing when I get back — I'm going to compile all the resource data from these five days into a report.
records.response_truth:
Yeah, that tracks. That's very you.

Make sure the part about the water source northeast gets in there — two hours on foot, downhill, rocky but manageable. That's the kind of thing that actually saves someone's life if this ever happens again.

And maybe include the bit about morale. Not in a soft way, just — practically speaking, the group nearly fell apart twice and both times it wasn't because of resources. That's worth noting if the report is supposed to be useful.
records.response_pred:
Sounds good to me, Leo. I'll help you organize it. Make sure to include the daily totals, any discrepancies, and observations about the terrain and weather patterns. We need to have a clear understanding of what we're dealing with and what resources we've got.

In the meantime, let's prioritize the immediate needs. I've spotted a few more areas that need repair on the shelter, and I think we should focus on those before they get worse.

Once we've got that sorted, we can move on to the signal. I've been thinking about using the mirror to reflect sunlight, but I want to run it by the rest of the group first.

And lastly, let's make sure we're all on the same page about rations. We don't want to waste anything, but we also can't afford to be hungry. I propose we stick to the original plan of two meals a day, but cut back on non-essential items like the crackers.

I'll start on the repairs, but I'll need your help with the report and the signal. Let's work together, okay?

records.utterance: Those flowers DaVinci drew on the beach… I never really understood what they were for. What practical purpose did they serve out here?
records.response_truth:
None. That's the point.

Not everything has to serve a purpose. The SOS got us found, maybe. The flowers kept DaVinci going. And DaVinci keeping going kept the rest of us going. So if you want to trace it back far enough and call that practical, fine. But I don't think that's why he drew them.

Some things are just — human. You know?

*looks at the boat on the horizon*

I still can't move, by the way. That's weird, right? I've been wanting this for five days and now I'm just standing here like an idiot.
records.response_pred: Well, I suppose they served as a form of communication. A way to convey thoughts and ideas without the need for words. They were a means to express the beauty and wonder of our surroundings, and to share that with others who might not have the opportunity to see it for themselves. While they may not have had a practical purpose in terms of survival, they undoubtedly added a touch of humanity and artistry to our otherwise harsh existence.

records.utterance: *His cheering stops. He looks over at you, notices you haven't moved, and the smile slowly fades. He waits.*
records.response_truth:
Yeah.

*still not moving*

Thanks for noticing.
records.response_pred: Hey, what's up? I'm sorry I didn't join in the cheering. I guess I've been a bit... preoccupied. But I'm here now, and I'm ready to help. Let's focus on what we've got ahead of us. We can celebrate later, once we've taken care of the task at hand. Let's get to work.

records.utterance: Rescue is here… they're waving us over. Are you going? I'll follow you.
records.response_truth:
Yeah. Let's go.

*takes a breath*

Come on then.
records.response_pred: Absolutely, let's go. I'll take the lead, you follow close behind. But remember, we should keep our wits about us. They might not know the entire story, so we should be ready to explain our situation and answer any questions they might have. They're our best chance, but we don't want to blow it. Let's go, Michelangelo.
